Silverymoon, the Welcoming City, was a powerful metropolis in the North and the thriving pinnacle of human culture, even amidst the wilderness of the Savage Frontier.[47][64] Though the Moon prized both education and art, especially music,[29][47] the Shining Towers also became home to many notable wizards, sorcerers, and other mages,[20] whose traditions came to define the Great Silver Hearth.[20][47] Its invisible Moonbridge was one such emblematic structure, as it was borne entirely from the Art.[29][47][65]

Known to the elves as Homehaven,[2] and translated from ancient Elven as Aerasumé (pronounced: /ˈeɪrɑːsuːˈmɛ/ AY-rah-soo-MEH[66]),[4] the city’s virtues, pursuits, and populace were grandly considered echoes of fabled Myth Drannor.[47][67] By the mid-to-late 14th century DR, this was largely attributed to the benevolence of Silvertowers’ then-ruler, High Lady Alustriel, who fostered unity between humans and demihumans within her city’s walls.[29][47][48] Later in her long rule, the Gem of the North even became the prime signatory state of the League of the Silver Marches and was viewed by many as the capital of the fledgeling nation.[45]

“

Description[]

Silverymoon was the largest city in the far lands of the Interior North,[68][47] and anywhere beyond Waterdeep,[29][48] but the bend of the River Rauvin split the Gem into two halves, one known as Northbank and the other Southbank.[69] The city once laid entirely on the northern shore,[29][47] the elder section,[69] and—even after expansion across the Moonbridge—most of its terrain still did.[47] From the shores of the Rauvin, Northbank's walls arced in a half circle to envelop Silverymoon,[29][70][71] being pierced by three gates at westerly, northerly, and easterly points, respectively.[70][71]

A large and open part of the city, known as the Market,[29][71] roughly divided Northbank further into western and eastern segments, as it reached from the wall to the city's Docks.[71] This harbor, wide and robust as it was,[29] was also surrounded by many shops.[71] The High Palace was located on the eastern side of Northbank, just inside the walls,[29][71] and protected by a proficient soldiery and mages, with varying levels of experience, who devoted themselves to the High Lady.[29][47] The city was also home to important temples of the Lathanderite,[29] Sorlyn, Oghmanyte, Helmite, Selûnite,[29][30] Mystran, Shiallian, Silvanite, and Tymoran faiths,[30] most of which could be found, alongside the houses of nobility, in the north-eastern area of the city.[71]

To reach across the river, the city employed its Moonbridge, which was invisible when not basked in the light of the moon. This magical span of force, however, could readily be dispelled using that same magic, allowing for a ship with too lofty a mast to pass without danger—or for foes on the Moonbridge to plummet unceremoniously into the river.[29][47]

Silvaeren expansion onto the other bank of the Rauvin began in the hundred years prior to 1358 DR, centred around the Moonbridge's southern terminus.[47] Originally, Southbank was an area for caravan business and warehouses, but it expanded to become nearly as large as Northbank, and was known for containing most of the schools that were part of the famous Conclave of Silverymoon.[19][20][72]

The city was also built atop numerous caverns, which resembled burrows,[73] and it was even rumored to hide many dwarven tunnels beneath its streets, filled with enough life to match that of the surface city.[71] Above ground, at least, Silverymoon had a dwarven quarter.[74]

Geography[]

The borders of Silverymoon's owned territory were distinguished using grey rocks which bore, engraved upon them, the city's Royal Badge.[75] To the immediate east of Silverymoon was Silverymoon Pass,[75][76] and the city of Sundabar beyond it,[64] while to the Gem's west hid the Heralds' Holdfast,[77] Mithral Hall, and Settlestone.[78] Far past them, Silverymoon was, if one went through Longsaddle, roughly 470 miles (760 kilometers) from the volcano of Mount Hotenow, both of which lay to the Moon's south-west.[79] Moving south would lead one first to Everlund,[64][80][81] and then to the north-western reaches of the awe-inspiring High Forest.[64] The town of Secomber, on the other side of the High Forest, was over 500 mi (800 km) away from the Moon.[82]

According to the stories told regarding Melazzar, a bard of Waterdeep, there laid another forested region between the Moon and the settlement of Triboar, far to the south-west; this forest was said to be the home of a number of sirens who lived around Dark Crag.[83] The popular narrative of Olithard's Tune also purported the existence of a bardic college in the forest to the south of Silverymoon, which the eponymous bard sought out.[84] However, he found only korreds, who bade him return to the Gem of the North.[85]

Geographical Features[]

Silverymoon was one of the few places where the River Rauvin was bridged, a feat also accomplished by the nearby cities of Sundabar, Everlund,[80][86] and Nesmé, as well as by Yartar and the Stone Bridge further south.[80] The lands north of the city also featured a hill which would become the final resting place of the ranger Lhoraie. She, alongside her daughter, was buried there by Hawkstone, a fellow ranger and Lhoraie's lover.[87]

Government[]

Internal Politics[]

When Alustriel was still in power, the politics of the city flowed smoothly. Legal disputes were delegated over in the morning with spare time left for private appointments with those who request them. In the evening, she declared any new laws or decrees, met with foreign delegations and oversaw policy debates. If these debates went on for too long, she would ask that the arguments be submitted to her in written form and then these would be copied and distributed freely to the citizenry. The public would themselves argue about the matter and then their written opinions were collected the next day and, guided by her own experience, Alustriel would cobble together the final policy.[88]

Royal Badge[]

The Royal Badge of Silverymoon bore two charges: a star and a crescent moon. The latter bowed to the right, with its thin, topmost point serving to cover the star, and both were borne on a field of royal blue. The star and moon, both, were instead colored silver.[29] It was similar in appearance to the mage sigil of the Lady Hope Alustriel, from which Silverymoon's coat of arms stemmed.[89]

External Politics[]

Allegiances[]

Silverymoon was—alongside such cities as Waterdeep, Sundabar, and Neverwinter—a member of the Lords' Alliance;[40][41][42][43] by 1357 DR, the Gem of the North could even be considered the most influential and sizeable city in the whole North, second only to the City of Splendors.[90] A year later, in 1358 DR, both Silverymoon and the Alliance were in talks with Everlund regarding the city's requests for the establishment and upkeep of a proper road, leading from their gates to Yartar, along the majority of the Evermoor Way.[81]

The Great Silver Hearth also maintained a positive relationship with the massive granary known as Goldenfields, despite the fact that Tolgar Anuvien, its ruler, quickly gained influence in the mid–14th century DR, on par with that of Lady Alustriel or the Neverwintian Lord Nasher.[90]

The Moon was also known as a stronghold of the enigmatic group known as the Harpers. Despite their clandestine nature, the organization was generally esteemed in the Savage Frontier,[44] as both High Lady Mage Alustriel,[91][92][93] and Khelben Blackstaff of Waterdeep,[44] openly acknowledged their membership in the organization.[44][92][93]

Silverymoon was also the leading city of the Confederation of the Silver Marches. Though still burgeoning, as of the late 14th century DR, and facing difficulties when cooperation was needed, it was nonetheless a common belief that the regions's cities would fall to the many enemies that surrounded them unless they managed to unite and fight as one.[45][46]

Adversaries[]

Though Silverymoon had many allies in the North, it also had its fair share of enemies. The Gem of the North was a primary foe of Grintharke and the demonic forces he gathered in Hellgate Keep,[44] as well as of King Graul of the Ice Mountain orcs. This last sought to conquer the North itself. Graul wished to see either the Moon or neighboring Sundabar as the first to fall under his grasping tyranny,[43] and so his orcs often raided against the two cities.[94]

This was a similar goal to that of the Arcane Brotherhood,[95] a small group of wizards and sorcerers who controlled the port city of Luskan from within their Hosttower of the Arcane.[95][96] Though the Brotherhood did not count Silverymoon among their worst enemies in 1358 DR,[44] this would later change, with the city, and the Silver Marches as a whole, being considered the main targets of the Brotherhood's quest for domination.[95]

Though not a primary foe of the Zhentarim in themselves, the forces of Zhentil Keep chose to begin their expansion into the North from Llorkh due to the city's distance from Silverymoon and Waterdeep both.[97] Enemies also lurked in the depths of Toril: the Underdark. In 1358 DR, an army of drow elves from the city of Menzoberranzan laid siege to Mithral Hall, a dwarven stronghold under the leadership of King Bruenor Battlehammer, and were driven back only with the combined efforts of Mithral Hall and Silverymoon.[98]

Trade[]

The bulk of Silverymoon's economy involved those finer pursuits of art and academia,[99] and it provided ample patronage to renowned schools of music. Magical studies were another primary industry of Silverymoon, as was the humbler craft of forestry.[47] Beyond these, much of the city's overland trade arrived from eastward Sundabar, bringing with it the riches of Citadel Adbar, a dwarven stronghold and the site of Faerûn's most prosperous mines.[64][100] Silverymoon was one of Sundabar's three most common, and important, trading partners.[101] These excursions through Silverymoon Pass, however, could be harrassed by bandits from the Nether Mountains.[75][94][102][103]

Beginning at some point in the 7th century DR,[note 4] and for many generations afterwards, the Moon suffered the depredations of the Chieftains in Gold, a blossoming culture of raiders.[102][103] By 1357 DR, the unceasing reavers of Silverymoon Pass were instead orc patrols originating from the Citadel of Many Arrows—which was, in itself, an everpresent threat.[75][81] It was said that the Citadel's king, Obould, was loyal to Graul of the Ice Mountains,[94] with such vast forces within the Citadel itself that it was impossible for Silverymoon to eradicate them, despite their attacks occasionally targeting the city gates of the Gem or of Sundabar.[75][81]

Given the isolated and dangerous nature of the land around Silverymoon, merchant caravans traveling to and from the city would sometimes hire the help of the Company of the Wolf, a capable adventuring company of the Northern Interior, as both guards and guides.[104] Though the city was also home to an outpost of the Six Coffers Market Priakos, a widespread and successful mercantile company,[105] much of the short, overland trade routes between the Gem of the North and Yartar were monopolized by the folk of Everlund.[81]

Goods & Currencies[]

Silverymoon minted its own coinage, in the denominations common elsewhere,[106] as well as its own, unique coin,[106][107] the moon.[107] Referred to, in the mid–14th century DR, as an electrum moon, it shone a metallic blue and was made into the shape of a crescent, being valued at 2 ep within Silverymoon's territory but only 1 ep beyond it.[106][108] It later became valued at 2gp and was accepted throughout the Silver Marches.[107]

Some of the good produced in and exported out of Silverymoon was a variety of white wine with a distinct blue tint: Silverymoon Blue. This wine became all the rage in Ravens Bluff in the late 14th century DR.[34]

Travel from Silverymoon[]

The Evermoor Way[]

The shortest of the Savage North's most common and prominent trade routes,[108][107] known as the Ever Road,[109] lay between Silverymoon and Everlund.[108][107] It departed from the Mulgate and passed through the western Nether Hills, as well as the old mines therein,[109] but was only 50 miles (80 kilometers) long,[107] meaning light horse riders could cross it in about two days. Caravans took five, whilst those on foot journeyed for roughly six days and six hours.[108]

The Ever Road was also a segment of the longer Evermoor Way, which linked Silverymoon to Yartar and Triboar, further southwest.[108][107] The former was 320 mi (510 km) away,[107] and the latter 400 mi (640 km),[citation needed] meaning departing wagons could reach them, respectively, in a tenday and eight days or in two tendays. As expected, horses were speedier, taking only seven days, four hours, and 48 minutes to arrive in Yartar, and eight days to get to Triboar. Foot travel was the slowest, with the route to Yartar stretched to two tendays, two days, and 12 hours, and to Triboar—that is, to walk the full length of the Evermoor Way—demanding nearly a month's travel, at two tendays and five days.[108]

The Long Road[]

Travelers hoping to reach the City of Splendors had to travel even further, traversing the Long Road from Triboar.[108][107] As Waterdeep stood a grand 600 mi (970 km) away from Silverymoon,[107] the total journey lasted a tenday, three days, four hours, and 48 minutes by horse; a month and three days by wagon; and a month, a tenday, a day, and six hours by foot.[108]

The Silver Road[]

The Silver Road, which led travel down Silverymoon Pass and to Sundabar beyond, was about 165 mi (266 km).[107] However, it was crossed in two days, nine hours, and 36 minutes by horses, and only six days by wagons; even those who braved the Pass on foot were able to arrive in Sundabar after seven and a half days of travel.[108] Though not linked to the Silver Road, Citadel Adbar itself, whose goods often traveled to the Great Silver Hearth by way of Sundabar, was ultimately about 355 mi (571 km) away from the Gem.[107]

The River Rauvin[]

The last of the established trade avenues that departed Silverymoon was the River Rauvin itself, whose current brought small barges towards the south-west.[108][107] A journey of 165 mi (266 km) led to the first major stop, Nesmé,[107] and lasted eight days and 16 hours. Yartar, now 375 mi (604 km) away,[107] could be reached slightly faster by barge than by wagon, as the trip was completed in a tenday, five days, and eight hours. Next were the Stone Bridge, passed in a tenday, nine days, and eight hours, and Ironford, a voyage that lasted two tendays, four days, and 16 hours. The last settlement where mainland travelers cast their anchor was Zundbridge, reached after two tendays, eight days, and sixteen hours of sailing—almost a month after departing Silverymoon.[108]

Defenses[]

Soldiery[]

“
For the good of all goodly folk!
”
— A Knight in Silver's rallying cry during the Battle of Keeper's Dale.[110]

Warriors and guardsmen aplenty were needed to defend the Welcoming City, and so it maintained both a militia and a standing army. An additional officer, the Sword-of-Coins, also commissioned bands of mercenaries for certain missions, such as routing any orcs between two regions of a map or destroying a known trollhold.[111][112]

However, for a myriad of reasons, the structure and name of the city's military changed multiple times over the course of its history. Such occurred at the whim of some of Silverymoon's early Warlords or as a consequence of orc hordes and plagues, including the one that struck the city in the Year of the Scourge, 1150 DR. Even upon Alustriel's election as High Lady Mage, they changed once more.[111][112]

Knights in Silver[]

Main article: Knights in Silver

The famed Knights in Silver were Silverymoon's standing army, and served as the foundation for the rest of the city's military.[47][29][111][112] Lionhearted to the last, their group numbered over 500,[47] and stood firm in the face of sundry threats—to the Shining Towers and to the greater North—as if they were no danger at all. Made up of gallant humans and half-elves, their enthusiasm was luckily not unearned, given their many victories in battles that others may have deemed hopeless. Occasionally, such triumphs depended on the assistance of two mysterious mages, the Mistmaster or the Shadowcloak; however, that fact did little to undermine the essential nature of the Knights' temerity and willpower.[29]

As the city's rapid cavalry, the Knights in Silver were primarily tasked with patrolling Silverymoon's lands, riding 50 miles (80 kilometers) away from the city proper,[note 5] in all directions,[111][112][113] even including Everlund.[114] The Knights could also, often, be found protecting the walls of the Gem of the North, striking out against marauding threats to the city, acting as Silverymoon's contribution to the Argent Legion, guarding caravans and encamped outsiders, or even escorting travelers of high import.[111][112]

Though they adopted the name, which originated in a ballad by Mintiper Moonsilver, the adventuring bard,[47][29][111][112] sometime circa the Year of the Bridle, 1349 DR,[111][112] the Knights in Silver were originally and informally known as the Silvershields. They also collaborated closely with a separate unit, the Steelshields, and together were the plainly-named Soldiers of Silverymoon who made up the Army of Silverymoon. Whereas the Silvershields were the cavalry, the Steelshields were instead motley fighters. With armor and armaments of a diverse sort, it was the latter's squads who initially dealt with training and patrolling beyond the city walls. However, this would become a responsibility of the Knights after they subsumed the Steelshields, who failed—despite many deaths in combat—to renew their ranks with enough new members.[111][112]

By 1372 DR, they were led by a paladin named Sernius Alathar,[20] and recruitment was overseen by Recruiting Master Mazillor Shatterstave, who scrutinized each potential applicant for suitability among their ranks.[115] Under Mazillor's watch the Knights in Silver rose to 704 members.[116]

The Spellguard[]

The Spellguard,[20] led by the half-elf wizard, Jorus Azuremantle,[117] was established in 1255 DR as a personal bodyguard for Alustriel herself. Over the intervening years, however, it grew into a city-wide force, spreading their duties between the High Palace and the rest of Silverymoon. By 1372 DR, the Spellguard numbered 32 members, 7 of which were Warders that oversaw the activities of the rest.[115]

In the nascent years of the Silver Marches, a wizard or sorcerer of the Spellguard always accompanied the Knights in Silver on their sojourns to patrol the vast wilderness surrounding Silverymoon.[113]

City Watch[]

Distinct from the Knights in Silver and the Spellguard,[111][112][114][118] the Moon also maintained two bodies of guards who were responsible for the city's quotidian security: the Moon Garrison and the Silverwatch.[114][118] They manned the gates and walls, watched over civic buildings, and policed the streets. Though not a formal matter of rank, both stood beneath the Knights and the Spellguard in terms of authority, which meant that any member of the former pair would obey an order given by a member of the latter pair without hesitation. Despite this, the Knights in Silver were not so vain as to avoid taking on ordinary guard duties, reinforcing the Moon Garrison and the Silverwatch on a rotating basis.[114]

The High Guard[]

Veterans of the Knights in Silver were the only people allowed to work as part of the High Guard, a subsection of Silverymoon's military that was solely and directly responsible for the security of the High Palace and its environs.[citation needed]

The Argent Legion[]

The army of the Confederation of the Silver Marches, composed of soldiers from every signatory of the confederation, also resided in Silverymoon for a time. This group, known as the Argent Legion, was led by a High Marshal. The first among these was a half-elven man of prodigious skill, both as a fighter and a wizard, by the name of Methrammar Aerasumé.[117]

Magical Defenses[]

Among the many magical instruments intended to defend the Gem of the North was the lost Arbatel, a tome crafted of beaten mithril plates. Orjalun, its white-haired creator, was one of the city's past rulers, and he enlisted the aid of the city's elven smiths in engraving the plates with spells that would assist in Silverymoon's continued protection, with the Arbatel acting as a permanent repertoire of his wisdom. It never served this purpose, however, for it was stolen soon after its crafting, taken by Orjalun's perfidious successor, Sepur.[119][120]

Silverymoon, at one point in its history, also produced a vast number of magical cloaks. They were only made in gray or brown, with an aged and featureless exterior, but they were capable of fitting themselves to any wearer with a form vaguely resembling a man in size.[121] Cloaks of reflection were one such item, invented by the mage Irentalar, that were bestowed upon any messenger or ranger employed in the name of Silverymoon.[122][123] Other cloaks made in the Gem included:

  • Cloaks of the shield, which projected an invisible force capable of variously acting like a wall of force or a weapon.[124][125]
  • Cloaks of symbiotic protection, which contained a strange substance that rendered their wearers colorblind while also protecting them from many molds, slimes, and spores.[124][125]
  • Cloaks of survival, which helped their wearers resist infections, among other things, and supplied them with fresh air when needed by enveloping their head.[125][126]
  • Cloaks of stars, which allowed the user to call upon spells contained within the cloak's stars by calling out the name of its creator, which was often Thalanta the Fair.[126][127]
  • Cloaks of many colors, which could glow and shift their hue to protect their wearers from confusing or blinding effects, such as prismatic wall, darkness, or color spray.[122][123]
  • Cloaks of fangs, which were, only once, able to shoot out darts of force by use of their activation word, and the name of their creator, Feerond.[121][123]
  • Cloaks of comfort, which ensured the wielder always experienced a pleasant temperature and kept them safe from certain spells, like heat metal or cone of cold.[121][128]
  • Cloaks of battle, which could grasp weapons attacking their wearers, parrying them, or even become cudgel-like implements in themselves.[121][128]

Silverymoon's Mythal[]

The city's Mythal was thought lost during the Spellplague, but it was merely dormant within the Moonbridge. With Mystra's Return, the mythal of Silverymoon blossomed out of the Moonbridge in all its former glory.[129]

History[]

Main article: History of Silverymoon

The history of Silverymoon long forewent the city it would eventually become, as its land had been sacred to the Lady of the Forest, Mielikki, and the Unicorn Queen, Lurue—the latter of which served as the city's namesake—since antiquity.[10][18] Faithful believed that the divinities first met in the time of legends, soon after Lurue's birth, by the shallow bend in the Rauvin where Mielikki had been sipping the waters. Even following their departure, Lurue was sometimes glimpsed around Silver Ford as a luminous unicorn, becoming a sign of good luck.[18]

However, the region was only populated some time after the fall of the Empire of Magic, first being settled by people of Netherese blood.[130] Thereafter, the Shining Towers humbly began as a simple bridge of wood and rope, known as Silverymoon Ford, that was built low across the river's shallows in the Year of Dreaming Dragons, 384 DR.[10][131][132] More than half a century passed before anything else was constructed in the area—only in 447 DR was the Moonsilver Inn established on the bridge's northern bank.[133] After that, a mere dozen years later, a lumber camp was erected, surrounding both bridge and inn. With this, Silverymoon Ford instead became known as Silver Village.[134]

It was not until the settlement had become Silverymoon Town,[18][53] centuries after Mielikki and Lurue had first graced the river ford,[18] that the pair returned once more. Taking the forms of a mortal ranger and her steed, they became enamored with the town and the Moonsilver Inn, for the people had worked alongside nature, rather than against it. This compelled the two deities to bless the inn,[18][53] keeping safe those with a good heart.[18]

Silverymoon became a city in Uktar 637 DR, when a stone wall was built around it for the first time and the first ruler of Silverymoon, High Mage Ecamane Truesilver, was elected.[135] He was instrumental in setting the foundation to the city's enduring fame of a center of lore and knowledge throughout the North. Truesilver founded a library and subsequent rulers of the city pursued artistic endeavors and further consolidated Silverymoon as a place where art, culture, lore, and magic were highly valued.[136]

After his death in 712 DR, and a reign of seventy-five years, Ecamane was succeeded by the second High Mage of Silverymoon, Aglanthol the Red, his nephew. When Myth Drannor fell in 714 DR, some prominent scholars found shelter in the city, but they were followed by the demons that destroyed their home. The then reigning High Mage, Aglanthol, perished in the ensuing fight in 719 DR. His successor, Ederan Nharimlur, by contrast, reigned for many years in peace. It was in his reign that the city almost doubled in size.[136]

Upon Ederan's death in 784 DR, his daughter Amaara Nharimlur became the High Mage of Silverymoon. In 815 DR, Elué Dualen arrived in the city and befriended Amaara and her sister Lynx. In 821 DR, Elué and Lynx established the Lady's College, the first open school for mages in Silverymoon to take students, not apprentices, and as payment for tutelage required an equal amount of time of service in defense of the city. In 843 DR Elué and other wizards created the Moonbridge, the city's most famous landmark[136] along with the wards of Silverymoon.[137] Eventually Elué became High Mage in 857 DR after Amaara left for Evermeet. Elué left the post in 876 DR with Lynx.[136]

The succession of High Mages was disrupted in 876 DR, when the warlord Lashtor, then commander of the city's army, took the city by force, destroying many important buildings and killing many wizards in the process. He could not remain in power for more than a year, however, as he was deposed by Tanalanthara Mytersaal, a mage also known as Lady Wolf. Lady Wolf sacrificed herself in 882 DR while fending off a horde of orcs.[138]

The next High Mage was chosen by the people of Silverymoon to be Tanisell the Cloaked, who during his reign strengthened the wards of the city and constructed the Vault of the Sages. In 920 DR the Keeper of the Vault of Sages, Nunivytt Threskaal, succeeded Tanisell.[139]

Beginning in the Year of the Cold Claws, 940 DR, Threskaal's reign bore witness to the Second Trollwar,[140] a conflict between the Waterdhavians and the Evermoor trolls. Until the armies of the civilized North were united by Aeroth, Silverymoon's champion and War Captain,[73][140][141] the fighting lasted a dozen years;[140] he was, however, able to lead them into the Trollmoors, with the war culminating in the nine day Long Battle and a victory for the Northern kingdoms. Before departing, Aeroth had been gifted Taragarth, the magical bastard sword forged long ago by the Gem's own Elfgar, and he wielded the blade so effectively as to earn it a second title as the Bloodbrand.[73][140][141]

Forty years after the end of the Second Trollwar, in the Year of the Scythe, 982 DR,[140] the mantle of Warlord was taken from Rayuth, who passed away in his old age, and given to his sadistic son, the arrogant Tulven. Aeroth, by then an older, white-bearded man, grieved the loss of his previous master. This sorrow, combined with his dislike for Tulven, cost Silverymoon its champion, who soon departed the Gem of the North with his wife and their six sons. Though incorrect, it was common myth that the Bloodbrand had been left behind in the city, perhaps lost in a labyrinthine cave beneath the streets or in some hidden hoard.[73][141]

Threskaal reigned for over a hundred years in peace until his death during 1050 DR.[139]

High Mage Orjalun was the next to take up the mantle of rulership and oversaw a reign that included the emergence of many famed mages such as Ahghairon and Bowgentle.[53][139]

Circa 1057 DR, the great dwarfhold of Citadel Felbarr, north-east of Silverymoon, was left behind by the Stout Folk. Very soon after, more than three thousand Silvaeren soldiers and other military officers were sent to occupy the keep,[75][81][142] seeking to annex it into an outpost to the nearby Ice Mountains and Coldwood. The Silvaeren hoped for mineral wealth, to bolster their coffers of gold and silver—the latter of which was in particularly low supply—but they also sought massive trees, which they thought to use in the building of their ships.[142] It was almost immediately after the Citadel was garrisoned that nearby orc tribes began skirmishing with the human forces.[75][81][142]

For 50 long years, Silverymoon held to Felbarr. This was only until they found themselves surrounded by an awful horde of orcs, which had charged the Citadel from Dead Orc Pass, the mountain cleft between the Silvaeren and the wilderness they sought to explore.[75][81][142] It was said that, so numerous were the orcs, it was impossible for the arrows flooding the sky to miss.[142] Though the onslaught was endless, and though the garrison's forces were decidedly not, they nonetheless shot everything they had into the orcs, missiles both mundane and magical. The Battle of Many Arrows, as it came to be known, lasted for over four months, with orc corpses piling higher and higher against the Citadel's walls until their still-unrelenting brethren finally crested the Silvaeren's defenses. The monsters butchered Silverymoon's people, and wrested control of their eastern base.[75][81][142]

Another disaster befell Silverymoon in the year 1150 DR, a plague against which nearly half the city's inhabitants perished.[53][139]

Orjalun's reign ended in the Year of the Long Watch, 1230 DR,[53] when he appointed Sepur, an apprentice of his, as the next High Mage.[53][119][120] It was to be a short reign, however, as Sepur left the city behind only two years later,[53][note 6] taking with him Orjalun's staff of Silverymoon and his Arbatel. Though Sepur's ultimate fate was unknown,[119][143] sagely Alphontras had heard of a strange sight in the nearby Evermoors: a tor had been seared, atop which rested only a broken staff.[119][143]

In the aftermath of Sepur's vanishing, an elected mayor ruled for the next three years;[53] this reign, in the Year of the Black Horde, 1235 DR, marked the first time that an enemy broke through the city walls since the office of High Mage was established. It was then that the army's commander, Khallos Shieldsunder, forcibly took control of the orc-sieged settlement, but the invading orcs were repelled only by the timely arrival of a combined force of elves and Harpers, led by Alustriel Silverhand and her sister Storm Silverhand.[144]

Alustriel subsequently became the city's only ruler to have been unanimously chosen by the people, and the only one to have reigned for so long.[144]

Silverymoon also became the home of the Amnian Princess Rasa Parhek, at some point after her birth in the Year of the Shattered Wall, 1271 DR; for her own protection, Rasa was entrusted to the High Lady Mage. It was also in the Gem of the North that the Princess met and married Dornar Steelsar, bearing him four children. However, she and her youngest were ultimately forced to leave the city in 1297 DR, after assassins from her homeland slew her husband and their two eldest children.[145]

Circa 1335 DR, Fythuera, a harpist, and her long-time husband, Hargun the Tall, himself a tradesman suffering from the shaking fever, had a child. Less than a year passed before they left the city, however; this left their son, named Narm Tamaraith, with no memories of this very earliest childhood.[146][147][148]

In the Year of the Wanderer, 1338 DR,[149] Silverymoon's court was visited by such figures as the renowned Elminster, Distyl of nearby Nesmé, the adventurer Urnen, and Abadda Moonglamaer. Carrying with him Susk, an infamously silent sword, the long-ago prince was challenged for it by Distyl, ultimately losing both his life and his weapon to the man. Though the blade was soon carried off, and lost in turn, by its new owner,[150][151][152][149] no one discovered that the fallen elf had secretly been a doppelganger.[149]

As part of the First Dragonspear War, the northerly village of Triboar was ransacked, such that, by Mirtul of the Year of the Worm, 1356 DR, its citizens, and those of similar, nearby towns, had fled. The Gem of the North was one city the refugees escaped to, as were Mirabar and some of the ports on the Sword Coast.[153]

By the Year of the Prince, 1357 DR, Silverymoon, as well as Sundabar and Citadel Adbar, had attacked the demons of Hellgate Keep, failed to reclaim the city, and faced direct offensives from the ghoul-hold themselves.[154][155] Though the fiends were turned back, the armed forces of these three cities, dwarves and humans alike, rallied together with those of nearby Everlund to block off Turnstone Pass, clashing near-endlessly to maintain their tenuous, if strategic, hold on the valley and keep their enemies from the northern cities.[77][155]

It was this same year that young Narm and his new bride, the spellfire-wielding Shandril Shessair, decided to leave behind the Dalelands and return to the Great Silver Hearth,[156][157][158] where they could be under the protection and tutelage of Alustriel.[156][157] This long voyage was encouraged by members of the Harpers, powerful wizards, and even the Knights of Myth Drannor.[158][159][160]

In Uktar of the Year of Shadows, 1358 DR, a terrible winter fell over the Gem of the North—worse even than the winter of 1357 DR, which had been the harshest season that most of the Silvaeren remembered. With the cold came monstrous assaults by winter wolves, devil dogs in enormous groups, and even the dreadful frost giants.[161]

Alustriel's reign officially ended in 1369 DR, when she stepped down, passing the city's supreme office to her trusted adviser Taern "Thunderspell" Hornblade. She assumed the title of High Lady of the Silver Marches in 1371 DR (the year the confederation was born) and became the leading figure of authority in the new-found confederation.[162]

When the Spellplague struck Silverymoon, it broke the city's mythal. All hope was not lost, however, as this meant it protected the city from the brunt of the Plague's effects.[163]

Silverymoon was involved in the destructive War of the Silver Marches between 1484 DR and 1485 DR, still under Taern's leadership as of 1485 DR.[164] However the city's lacklustre efforts to help Sundabar during the war tarnished its reputation.[165][166]

By 1489 DR, High Mage Taern Hornblade had stepped down as ruler of the city and Methrammar Aerasumé took over as Lord of Silverymoon. Despite this, Taern still spoke for the city among the Lords' Alliance.[27]

Notable Locations[]

Silverymoon was home to a variety of magical colleges, including one for druids. Inhabitants[]

The most exemplary bards in the North were raised from the refined and well-educated stock of the Great Silver Hearth,[174] and many tutors of the Art, independent of the city's colleges, also made their homes here. The city was even said to have a minor thieves' guild, one possibly allied with the secretive Harpers.[167] The Netherese blood common in Silverymoon also meant many of its people had fair skin paired with dark locks.[175] Other notable denizens of Silverymoon included:

  • Alustriel[149][150][151][152][176][177][178][179][180][181][182]
  • Ahghairon: The savior of Waterdeep and the creator of its Lords was said to be Silvaeren.[183]
  • Bowgentle:[184] Of the many mages of the North, Bowgentle was among the most legendary. His years of adventuring and expertise in the Art did nothing to diminish his natural kindness.[185][186]
  • Dauntus: This wizard, known as the Seneschal of Silverymoon, notably collaborated with Askrim "The Bold", the Neverwintian Grand Alchemist. Together, they wrote an extensive magical recipe named The Making of a Homonculous.[187][188]
  • Dzance: An adventurous ranger, who retired to the Lady's Court at some point in the early-to-mid 14th century DR. He brought with him Dzance's guardian, a magical shield recovered from fabled Gauntlgrym, and gifted it to one of the city's budding knights, Belpir—who promptly left on an adventure of his own.[189][190]
  • Fret
  • Illius: A Silvaeren sorcerer and adventurer trained by Khelben of Waterdeep. Illius traveled as far as Damara and Chult in his and his party's quest to end the conflict between a slaad lord and a githyanki general.[191]
  • Liantha: One of the city's Tymoran priestesses, the woman left the Gem of the North behind sometime during Hammer of 1357 DR. With a group of adventurers, she embarked towards the Anauroch, hoping to find a route through—and past—the desert, so as to arrive in the Dalelands and Cormyr, which lay beyond.[192]
  • Methrammar Aerasumé
  • Nyral Sunsdottir: Raised by relatives of her mother, Nyral was a half-elven woman who keenly employed her sword of dancing in combat.[193]
  • Perendra Raslemtar: A Tethyrian noble who trained and matured in Silverymoon, under the watch of Alustriel, before departing the city some years before 1357 DR. It was also during this time that she befriended Harnoster, a ki-rin.[194]
  • Ransair: A local sage who once gave a famous warning to aventurers.[195]
  • Taern Hornblade
  • Tuirlagh "Foehammer" Nundass: A local adventurer who operated some centuries prior to the mid–14th century DR, known for his having slain the creature that gave Yellow Snake Pass its name.[196]

Culture[]

Religion[]

The Silvaeren tended to worship deities that aligned themselves with the Gem of the North's pursuits—which focused on artistry, beauty, and academia—as well as those that matched their dependence on the nearby woods, like Shiallia, Silvanus, and Mielikki.[31] The city also had temples to Lathander,[29] Milil, Oghma, Helm, Selûne,[29][30] Mystra, Tymora,[30] and even Shar,[197][198] but it notably outlawed the Church of Cyric.[33]

Festivals & Holidays[]

Silvertowers observed not only the standard festivals of the Calendar of Harptos, including Greengrass,[199] Midsummer,[197][200][201] and Shieldmeet,[26][197][200] but also many more, given its tolerant and cosmopolitan nature. Notable among these were the individual rites—held by each of the local temples—and citywide festivities that took place leading up to Midsummer. Each day of the tenday prior, the Silvaeren respected a distinct festival.[197][200][202] During the mid-14th century DR,[note 8] these events included:

Oldcasks
The first festival, which took place on Flamerule 21, was a day when much fine wine and ale was sold. In preparation for the upcoming festivities, vendors imported unique vintages or offered sales, doing so from tables set up by their front doors. Moreover, all of the Welcoming City's temples brought in clergy and prepared spell scrolls so as to freely cleanse any liquids brought to them, between dusk and dawn, of poisons.[197][202]
Cloakswirl
The second day was one for purchasing costumes, accessories, and clothing—but not any headwear, masks, or cosmetics, which were considered unlucky—to be used during the upcoming festivals. Similar to Oldcasks, Cloakswirl was a day where many shops brought their tables and wares directly out onto the street, and, after dusk, tradition demanded that local taverns and inns stage dramatic readings or short plays.[197][203]
Moondown
The only religious celebration enjoyed across the Moon,[197][202] the day initially carried on as normal for most—excepting Sharran temples, which were closed all day. After highsun, the Silvaeren would begin by bathing and changing into clothing they had never before worn; after dusk, a solemn Selûnite ritual took place. Known as a Moondance, priests of the Night White Lady led processions of silent and unhurried dancers, who offered refreshments to the citizenry. It was also a night to remember loved ones that had recently passed away, and to murmur wishes up towards the moon.[197][198]
Masks
During the day of the fourth festival, Silvaeren crafters now sold what had previously, during Cloakswirl, been considered unlucky: highly detailed masks and the like, typically at exorbitant prices. These were to be used from then on until the end of Midsummer, as the revels that began on Masks night continued, perpetually, throughout the following days. During the reign of the Shining Lady, Alustriel often paid musicians a sum of 25 gp, who would then play on the streets of Silverymoon as parties or individuals.[197][198]
Eskelter
The fifth festival began as a typical day of work, akin to Moondown, until the Skull Run began at highsun. This was a massive, citywide chase, wherein Skull Runners—individual donning skull-like masks and, typically, nothing else but grease—attempted to reach the Moonbridge from one of the city's gates. Both successful Skull Runners and chasers, however, were afforded prizes by Alustriel. By dusk, Eskelter became instead about gathering with old friends, reminiscing on the previous year and toasting those who could not be present, as well as preparing their upcoming dealings.[197][198]
Claws
The second half of Silverymoon's summer festivals began with Claws, a day where the Silvaeren took to the streets in elaborate monster costumes—the most popular forms of which were owlbears and dragons. The city's youth often fell alongside these monstrous parades, heading to the city's taverns,[197][198] where all were provided with free, if diluted, drinks,[197][204] while the unmasked costume wearers were also given complimentary food.[197][205] The feasting lasted until the early morning, during which many tall tales were spread regarding fearsome beasts, terrible undead, or the Realms Below.[197][204]
Glarth
Glarth was a day of feasting, not revelry, and appropriately known by the citizenry as Fullbelly. In the morning, the High Palace sent decorated wagons, filled with food to be freely taken, to circulate throughout the city, while lonesome individuals—such as guests to Silvertowers—gathered in taverns and inns or were taken into family homes to share in the day's fare. After such filling meals, most simply drowsed, wiling away the rest of the day with idle conversation.[200][204]
Oamaurae
The next day of festivities rarely began until highsun, as most Silvaeren slept deeply after the repasts of Fullbelly. Per tradition, however, Oamaurae was a day to enjoy the theater. Performances occurred everywhere: on the streets, in personal homes, at inns, taverns, playhouses, or even acting grounds beyond the city walls. Many new drinks, ballads, and plays were also unveiled on Oamaurae. Afterwards, individuals continued the festival at home by reciting stories and prose, punctuating it all with a feast of desserts before bedding down.[200][204]
Clearsight
The penultimate summer festival of Silverymoon began, as Moondown and Eskelter did, at highsun. The city's stores closed for the festivities, giving way to a day full of discussion and looking ahead as personal plans were made, agreements were discussed with partners or employees, and worldly news was shared. Given the day's closures, people also had a chance to meet with any investors needed for their upcoming endeavors.[200][204]
Amalree’s Pleasure
The Pleasure took place on Flamerule 30 and was a day dedicated to the eponymous Amalree, a Silvaeren dancer. It was a time for carefree dancing and coquetry, though even those too injured or old to partake enjoyed watching, drinking wine, and engaging themselves with board games. Placing bets on such games became increasingly common, with much money wagered by the end of Amalree's Pleasure.[200][204]
Feast of Love
Ultimately, these culminated in the Feast of Love, which was the festival taking place on Midsummer. It began, once more, with shops closing at highsun, leading to people eating sumptous meals at home and engaging in public debauchery on the streets of Silverymoon.[200][204] Trysts and revealing garments were common, and the various faithful of the city freely offered their spells to cure any diseases incurred. By moonrise, Alustriel personally led a Hunt of Maidens, chasing a masked individual through a series of gardens, and many of the wealthier members of the citizenry hosted risqué parties.[200][206]

Every four years, the Gem of the North also observed Shieldmeet. As with most other places in Faerûn, it was a day where the Silvaeren could speak plainly with their rulers, discussing gossip, offering warnings, answering questions, or simply complaining. The citizenry knew there was no reprisal for what they said, while the High Mage was additionally protected from certain spells, arrows, or the like. Often, useful informants were called to meet again soon after Shieldmeet.[200][206]

Deals and agreements were often renewed on Shieldmeet, typically haven been established or assessed a few days prior, during Clearsight. This applied not only to the Silvaeren rulership, but also to any in the business of transactions or rentings, masters and their apprentices, members of certain organizations, and merchants. The last element to a Silvaeren Shieldmeet were the various tournaments and contests that took place, be they using traditional armaments or the Art.[200][206]

The Silvaeren were widely entertained by these competitions, often betting on them. Prizes were offered by sponsors, such as wealthy citizens or merchants, and many hedge wizards or adventurers took part in the Shieldmeet contests, successfully impressing patrons who might employ them. If permission was granted by Alustriel or Taern Hornblade, these duels could also serve as resolutions to legal issues, personal disputes, or merely the competitors' fury, but such demanded that wizards of the Spellguard watch over the affair, and was rare to see.[200][206]

Any injuries sustained were cared for and healed, without charge, by visiting clerics and the local temples. All of which led to the festival's climax, wherein plays and music were performed across the city's guildhouses, taverns, clubs, and inns. Much food was enjoyed, such as candies, pastries, and honeycakes, as was sweetened wine and mead. As all were aware, normalcy returned on the following day, so the wisest Silvaeren avoided staying late or getting overly drunk—even so, some spent the night in revel, and were forced to suffer a hangover while working on the follwing day.[200][206]
